title: Quantum startup ZuriQ partners with Infineon for development of scalable quantum chips
source_used: The Quantum Insider (joint Infineon and ZuriQ press release, dated 7 Oct 2026); Data Center Dynamics page returned HTTP 403
key_facts: Infineon Technologies and ZuriQ AG, a Swiss quantum computing company spun out of ETH Zurich, announced an expanded collaboration on scalable quantum computing hardware.
Earlier joint work trapped a 3x3 array of nine individually controlled ions, which the release calls the largest two-dimensional array of its kind to date.
The next step is to scale the technology to significantly larger qubit counts.
ZuriQ uses a natively two-dimensional Penning micro-trap architecture that moves ions across the chip with electric and magnetic fields, avoiding complex junctions.
Infineon contributes semiconductor manufacturing, advanced packaging and integrated photonics.
The release gives no timeline, funding amount or qubit target.
quote_evidence: Previous development work by ZuriQ and Infineon demonstrated the feasibility of this novel architecture by trapping a 3×3 array of nine individually controlled ions, achieving the largest two-dimensional array of its kind to date.
The next step in the partnership is to scale the technology to significantly larger qubit counts.
why_it_matters_hint: A chip manufacturer and a quantum startup are working to make a 2D trapped-ion design manufacturable.
